account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 an earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey, at a depth of roughly 40 km. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 5.1, and AFAD, Turkey's disaster and emergency agency, put it at 5.3. Google had introduced its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Turkey in June 2021. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day that the system sent Android users an audible and visual alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake seconds before the shaking. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage or injuries. İndigo Dergisi claimed on 5 January that the alert came about a minute ahead. On 7 January 2022 Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds. It also reported that most users who posted about the alert said that they panicked. On 18 January 2022 NTV repeated the figure of about a minute. On 3 February 2022 Google said that the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir. In July 2023 BBC Newsnight reported that its reporters had spoken with hundreds of Android users in Adana, Iskenderun and Osmaniye. They found no one who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023. Google's product lead told the BBC that he was confident that the system fired and sent alerts. A study by Google staff, published on 11 August 2026, reports that the system sent alerts to more than 16 million users for the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake of 23 April 2025.

ai_role.statement: The alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake and estimate its size. Alerts were pushed to phones in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower S-waves. Google's own descriptions of this process do not use the words AI or machine learning. The OECD Monitor classifies it as an AI system doing event detection and forecasting, and the 2025 Science paper calls it smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. The reported lead time varies by outlet (seconds, about 10 seconds, about one minute); Google promises seconds.

paired_incident.basis: Both cases concern the Android Earthquake Alerts System warning phone users in Turkey before shaking arrives, and the people at stake are residents exposed to the earthquake.
paired_incident.title: Google Android Earthquake Alerts System Reportedly Underestimated Kahramanmaraş Earthquake and Failed to Send Urgent Warnings to Millions

display.answer: A BBC Newsnight investigation found no one in three Turkish cities who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of the deadly 6 February 2023 earthquake. Google's product lead told the BBC that he was confident that the system fired and sent alerts. Google did not give the BBC evidence that the alerts were widely received.

fields.taxonomy_note: The alert arrived seconds before shaking, but no protective action by a recipient and no harm are documented.

fields.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 an earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey, at a depth of roughly 40 km. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 5.1, and AFAD, Turkey's disaster and emergency agency, put it at 5.3. Google had introduced its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Turkey in June 2021. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day that the system sent Android users an audible and visual alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake seconds before the shaking. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage or injuries. İndigo Dergisi claimed on 5 January that the alert came about a minute ahead. On 7 January 2022 Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds. It also reported that most users who posted about the alert said that they panicked. On 18 January 2022 NTV repeated the figure of about a minute. On 3 February 2022 Google said that the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir. In July 2023 BBC Newsnight reported that its reporters had spoken with hundreds of Android users in Adana, Iskenderun and Osmaniye. They found no one who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023. Google's product lead told the BBC that he was confident that the system fired and sent alerts. A study by Google staff, published on 11 August 2026, reports that the system sent alerts to more than 16 million users for the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake of 23 April 2025.

display.answer: The alert was a single warning before one quake. The recorded follow-up is a BBC Newsnight investigation of July 2023, which found no one in three Turkish cities who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023.

fields.purpose: Built to detect earthquakes from Android phones' accelerometers and alert users in the expected shaking zone seconds before the slower destructive waves arrive. It covers quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above. This alert was that intended function.

must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. Hürriyet reported on 7 January 2022 that most users who posted about the Alanya alert said they panicked
The phone must have location and the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled
produced_by: A magnitude 5.1 (AFAD 5.3) quake above the 4.5 alert threshold, centered about 57 km offshore and roughly 40 km deep. So the push alert could outrun the slower S-waves to the coast.

Enough Android phones near the epicenter with Earthquake Alerts on to trigger Google's server-side detection. Per Google's 3 February 2022 presentation it runs on Android 5.0 and later and users can switch it off.

fields.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 an earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey, at a depth of roughly 40 km. The U.S. Geological Survey put its magnitude at 5.1, and AFAD, Turkey's disaster and emergency agency, put it at 5.3. Google had introduced its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Turkey in June 2021. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day that the system sent Android users an audible and visual alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake seconds before the shaking. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage or injuries. İndigo Dergisi claimed on 5 January that the alert came about a minute ahead. On 7 January 2022 Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds. It also reported that most users who posted about the alert said that they panicked. On 18 January 2022 NTV repeated the figure of about a minute. On 3 February 2022 Google said that the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir. In July 2023 BBC Newsnight reported that its reporters had spoken with hundreds of Android users in Adana, Iskenderun and Osmaniye. They found no one who received a warning from the same system before the main shock of 6 February 2023. Google's product lead told the BBC that he was confident that the system fired and sent alerts. A study by Google staff, published on 11 August 2026, reports that the system sent alerts to more than 16 million users for the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake of 23 April 2025.
fields.summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System warned Android users near Alanya, Turkey, seconds before a magnitude 5.1 offshore quake on 5 January 2022.

mapping.basis_excerpt: The alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake and estimate its size. Alerts were pushed to phones in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower S-waves. Google's own descriptions of this process do not use the words AI or machine learning. The OECD Monitor classifies it as an AI system doing event detection and forecasting, and the 2025 Science paper calls it smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. The reported lead time varies by outlet (seconds, about 10 seconds, about one minute); Google promises seconds.

echoes.setting: Kahramanmaraş (Pazarcık) M7.8 earthquake, southern Turkey: BBC reporters found no Android user who received a warning before the main shock
Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake near Istanbul: a study by Google staff reports that the system alerted more than 16 million users, with a median warning of 56 seconds for weak shaking

must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. Hürriyet reported on 7 January 2022 that most users who posted about the Alanya alert said they panicked
The phone must have location and the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled
produced_by: A magnitude 5.1 (AFAD 5.3) quake above the 4.5 alert threshold, centered about 57 km offshore and roughly 40 km deep. So the push alert could outrun the slower S-waves to the coast.

Enough Android phones near the epicenter with Earthquake Alerts on to trigger Google's server-side detection. Per Google's 3 February 2022 presentation it runs on Android 5.0 and later and users can switch it off.
Crowdsourced phone detection was the only input: Google partners with the ShakeAlert seismic network only in California, Oregon and Washington

purpose: Built to detect earthquakes from Android phones' accelerometers and alert users in the expected shaking zone seconds before the slower destructive waves arrive. It covers quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above. This alert was that intended function.

ratings.reason: An unstated number of Android users near Alanya received a few seconds' notice of a quake that AFAD and the district governor said caused no damage or injuries. No recipient is reported to have taken protective action, and Hürriyet reported on 7 January 2022 that most users who posted about the alert said that they panicked.
